_comment: Read by scripts/build_halo.py and api/screen.js. Value floors must match on both sides or a path's verdict depends on which half an edge falls in. Fanout differs on purpose: see _rules.
_rules: Edges below min_edge_usd are ignored, on both sides of every path. This is what stops address-poisoning dust from tainting an arbitrary wallet.

Every edge is valued in dollars at the price on the day it happened. Stablecoins are one-to-one; ETH and BTC pegged assets use daily closes from data/prices.json. A token that cannot be valued is ignored entirely, which is what keeps spam tokens out.

A single USD floor replaced the earlier per-asset unit floors. Under those, every qualifying token transfer weighed the same regardless of size, so a $1,000 and a $50,000,000 USDC transfer were indistinguishable, and thresholds in ETH were blind to the stablecoin flows that carry most laundering volume.

Service nodes (exchanges, bridges, mixers, from data/services.json), contracts, and nodes above high_degree_tx_count are terminal: they can be a match but never an intermediary. Without this rule every address that has ever used Binance is three hops from Lazarus.
max_fanout_build is a compute budget, not a rule about exposure. At query time the same check is a dictionary lookup and costs nothing, so max_fanout_query is set far higher.
Exposure value is the smallest edge along the path, not the largest. A wallet that received $500,000 from an intermediary that received $30 from a Lazarus address is exposed to $30, not $500,000.
